1. Short title extent and
commencement------(1) This Act may be called the Presidential Election Act,

CHAPTER I
PRELIMINARY
2. Definition-----In this
Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,-
(a) "
Article " means an Article of the Constitution ;
(b) "
ballot paper account" means a ballot paper ac count prepared under
sub-section (3) of section 36 ;
(c) "
candidate " means a person proposed as a candi date for election to the
office of President ;
(d) "
Commission " means the Election Commission constituted under Article 153;
(e) "
Commissioner " means the Chief Election Com missioner appointed under
Article 147 ;
(f) "
contesting candidate " means a candidate who has been validly nominated
and has not withdrawn his candidature ;
(g) "election
" means an election to the office of Presi dent held under this Act ;
(h) "
election agent " means an election agent appointed by a candidate under
section 20 and, where no such appointment is made, the candidate acting as his
own election agent ;
(i) "
elector " (Subs. by the Presidential Election
(Amdt.) Ordinance, 1964 (11 of 1964), s. 2, for ", in relation to an
election, means a person who, on the date of the notification under section 3
for such election,".)[means a person who] is a member of the
Electoral College of Pakistan constituted under the Electoral College Act, 1964
;
(j) "
electors' list " means a list of electors mentioned in section 25 ;
(k) "joint
sitting" means a joint sitting of members of the National Assembly and of
the Provincial Assemb lies or, if the National Assembly stands dissolved, of
the Provincial Assemblies only, convened under Article 166 or Article 167 ;
(l) "
nomination day " means the day specified in the notification under section
5 ;
(m) "
polling agent " means a polling agent appointed under section 21 ;
(n) "
prescribed " means prescribed by rules ;
(o) "
returned candidate " means a candidate who has been declared elected to
the office of President under section 18 or section 38 ;
(p) "
Returning Officer " means the Commissioner and includes an Assistant
Returning Officer performing any function which he is authorised to perform
under sub-section (2) of section 4 ;
(q) " rules
" means rules made under this Act ; and
(r) "
Speaker " means the Speaker of the National Assembly of Pakistan and, in
his absence, the senior of the Deputy Speakers and, in the absence of both, the
other Deputy Speaker.

3. Notification for
election-------(1) For the purpose of an election, the Commission shall, by
notification in the official Gazette, call upon the electors f` to elect a
President before such date as may be specified in the notification so that the
election is completed within the period specified in Article 165.
(2) The notification under
sub-section (1) shall be issued,-
(a) in the case of
an election to fill a vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of
President, as soon as may be after the commence ment of the period of one
hundred and twenty days specified in clause (2) of Article 165 ;
(b) in the case
of an election to fill a vacancy Occur ring by reason of the dissolution of the
National Assembly, as soon as may be after the date of such dissolution ;
(c) in the case
of an election to fill a vacancy occurring by reason of death, resignation,
impeachment, removal or the failure of an elected person to enter upon his
office, as soon as may be after the occurrence of such vacancy ; and
(d) in the case
of new election under clause (6) of Article 165 where a person validly
nominated as a candidate for election dies before the completion of the
election, as soon as may be after the death of such person.

returning Officer------(1) For the purpose of an election, the Commission
shall, with the approval of the President, appoint at least one Assistant
Returning Officer for each Province.
(2) Subject to any rules made in
this behalf, or any direction given by the Commission, an Assistant Returning
Officer may perform all or any of the functions of the Returning Officer.

6. Nomination------( Amended in its application to Tribal Areas, vide
Notifications No. D- 2133-FI (Sol)/64, dated the 21st November, 1964, see Gaz.
of P., 1964, Ext., p. 592u.)(1) Any elector may propose or second the
name of any person qualified for election to the office of President.
(2) A person is qualified. to be
elected as President if he-
(a) is a Muslim
;
(b) has attained
the age of thirty-five years ; and
(c) is qualified
to be elected as a member of the National Assembly.
(3) Every proposal shall be made
by a separate nomina tion paper in the prescribed form, signed by the proposer
and the seconder, and such form shall contain-
(a) a
declaration signed by the candidate that he has consented to the nomination and
that he is not sub ject to any disqualification for being elected as President,
and such declaration shall .specify the district and the electoral unit in
which he is a. voter ; and
(b) an oath in
the following form, namely
OATH
" I (A, B)
having been proposed as a candidate for elec tion to the office of President
swear in the name of Allah that I will always uphold the sovereignty and
integrity of Pakistan and shall bear true faith and allegiance to the
Constitution of Pakistan as by law established."
(4) Every nomination paper shall
be delivered on or be fore the nomination day by the candidate, his proposer or
secon der or an agent authorised in this behalf in writing by the can didate,
to the Returning Officer who shall acknowledge' the re ceipt of the nomination
paper in writing specifying the date and time of receipt.
(5) A person may be nominated by
more than one nomi nation paper
Provided that no elector shall
subscribe to more than one nomination paper whether as proposer or seconder and
if any elector subscribes to more than one nomination paper all such nomination
papers, except the one received first by the Returning Officer, shall be void.
(6) The Returning Officer shall
endorse on the nomination paper the name of the person presenting it and the
date and time of its receipt.
(7) The Returning Officer shall
cause to be affixed at some conspicuous place in his office a notice of every
nomination paper received by him containing the particulars of the candidate,
his proposer and seconder as shown in the nomination paper.

7. Doposit-(1) Subject to
the provisions of sub-section (2) no nomination paper shall be accepted unless-
(a) a sum of
five thousand rupees is deposited in cash with the Returning Officer by the
candidate or by any person on his behalf at the time of its delivery ; or
(b) it is
accompanied by a receipt showing that a sum as aforesaid has been deposited in
favour of the Commission by the candidate or by any person on his behalf at any
branch of the National Bank of Pakistan or at a Government Treasury.
(2) Not more than one deposit
under sub-section (1) shall be required in the case of any person who has been
nominated as a candidate by more than one nomination paper.

8. Scrutiny-------(1) The
candidates, their proposers and seconders, and one person authorised in this
behalf by each candidate, may attend the scrutiny of the nomination papers, and
the Returning Officer shall give them reasonable opportunity for examining the
nomination papers delivered to him under section 6.
(2) The Returning Officer shall,
in the presence of the persons attending the scrutiny under sub-section (1),
examine the nomination papers and decide any objection raised by any such
person to any nomination.
(3) The Returning Officer may,
either of his own motion or upon any objection, conduct such summary inquiry as
he may think fit and reject any nomination paper if he is satisfied that (a) the candidate is not qualifies under the
Constitution to be elected as President ;
(b) the
candidate is disqualified from being, or being elected as a member of an
elective body under the Elective Bodies (Disqualification) Order, 1959, or any
other law for the time being in force ;
(c) the proposer
or the seconder is not an elector ;
(d) any
provision of section 6 or section 7 has not been complied with ; or
(e) the
signature of the proposer or the seconder is not genuine:
Provided that--
(i) the rejection of a nomination
paper shall not
Amended in its application to
Tribal Areas, vide Notifn. No. D-2133 FI (Sol)/64, dated the 21st November,
1964, see Gaz. of P., 1964, Ext., p. 592u, invalidate the nomination of a
candidate by any other valid nomination paper ;
(ii) the Returning Officer shall
not reject a nomi nation paper on the ground of any defect which is not of a
substantial nature, and may allow such defect to be remedied forthwith ; and
(iii) the Returning Officer shall
not enquire into the correctness or validity of any entry in the electoral roll
for an electoral unit prepared under the Electoral College Act, 1964, or in the
electors list. IV of 1964.
(4) The Returning Officer shall
endorse on every nomina tion paper his decision, accepting or rejecting it, and
shall, in the case of rejection, record a brief statement of reasons therefor.
(5) Where the nomination of a
candidate has been rejected by the Returning Officer, an appeal shall lie
within the prescribed period to the Commission ; and any order passed by the
Com mission on such appeal shall be final.

candidate who has been validly nominated may within the prescribed period by
notice in writing signed by him and delivered to the Returning Officer either

by such candidate, withdraw his candidature.
(2) A notice of withdrawal under

11. Information to speaker
where action under Article 166 or 167 is necessary-----If, after withdrawal
of candidature, if any, the Re turning Officer finds that ---
(a) a person who
is, and has for a continuous period of more than eight years been, holding
office as Presi dent is a validly nominated candidate, or
(b) the number
of validly nominated candidates, ex cluding the candidate who is holding the
office of President, exceeds three, he shall forthwith make a report to that
effect to the Commis sioner ; and the Commissioner shall, except when a
Provincial Assembly stands dissolved, so inform the Speaker who, there upon,
shall forthwith convene a joint sitting.

Procedure for joint sitting

12. Procedure for joint
sitting-------(1) The Speaker shall fix the time and place for the joint
sitting ; and the Secretary of the National Assembly shall issue a notice of
such sitting to every member of the National Assembly and the Provincial
Assemblies specifying therein the time and place so fixed.
(2) The Speaker, and, in his
absence, a person elected by the members present from amongst themselves, shall
preside at the joint sitting.
(3) One hundred and twenty
members or, where the National Assembly stands dissolved, eighty members shall
constitute the quorum at the joint sitting.
(4) The Speaker or the person
presiding at the joint sitting shall conduct the proceedings thereof so as to
ensure the orderly and expeditious disposal of its business giving every
candidate, as far as practicable, equal opportunity of participating at the
sitting and of addressing, and being questioned by, the members present and, in
so conducting may-
(a) restrict the
number of questions that may be put to each candidate or by a member ;
(b) disallow any
question which contravenes sub-section (5) or is otherwise irrelevant ; and
(c) disallow any
candidate to proceed with his speech which contravenes sub-section (6).
(5) No member shall ask any
candidate any question which has no bearing on his candidature or which is
calculated to scandalize any candidate.
(6) No candidate shall in his
address at the joint sitting ---
(i) refer to any matter which has
no bearing on his candidature, or which is sub judice in any court in Pakistan
;
(ii) make any remark which
reflects upon the personal conduct of the President, a Judge of the Supreme
Court or of a High Court ;
(iii) make any statement which is
defamatory of, or is calculated to scandalize, any other candidate ; or
(iv) make use of offensive,
abusive or vulgar expressions.
(7) The selection of three
candidates by secret ballot under clause (2) of Article 167 shall be made by
the method of single non-transferable vote, that is, each member shall have
only one vote to be cast in favour of one candidate and the three candidates
receiving the highest number of votes shall be selected.
(8) A person entitled to take
part in the proceedings of a joint sitting shall not be liable to any
proceedings in any court in respect of anything said by him or any vote given
by him in a joint sitting.
(9) No proceeding in a joint
sitting shall be invalid by reason only that a person who was not entitled to
do so was present at or voted or otherwise participated in the proceedings.

13. Publication of names of
selected candidates-----(1) The Speaker shall, with reasonable despatch,
communicate to the Commissioner whether or not the candida ture of the
President has been approved under Article 166, and also the names of the
candidates selected under Article 167, and the Commissioner shall expeditiously
transmit such infor mation to the Returning Officer.
(2) The Returning Officer shall
thereupon publish in the official Gazette, in a single list-
(i) the name of the President if
he is a candidate, and, where his candidature required approval under Article
166, if such candidature has been approved thereunder ; and
(ii) the names of the other
validly nominated candidates or, where the number of such candidates exceeds
three, the names of such of the three candidates as have been selected under
Article 167.

15. Retirement from election
etc------(1) A contesting candidate may, by notice in writing, signed by
him and delivered, on any day not later than seven days before the polling day,
to the Returning Officer, either by such candidate in person or by an agent
authorised in this behalf in writing by such candidate, retire from the
election.
(2) A notice of retirement under
sub-section (1) shall, in no circumstances, be open to cancellation.
(3) On receiving a notice of
retirement under sub-section (1), the Returning Officer shall, if he is
satisfied that the signature on the notice is that of the candidate, cause a
copy of the notice to be affixed at some conspicuous place in his office and
also publish it in the official Gazette.
(4) A candidate in respect of
whom a notice of retirement has been published under sub-section (3) shall
cease to be a contesting candidate.

16. Death of a candidate------(1)
If a person validly nominated as a candidate who has not withdrawn his
candidature or has not retired from elec tion dies before the completion of the
election, the Returning Officer shall, by public notice, terminate the
proceedings relating to the election and make a report to the Commissioner.
(2) Where any proceedings have
been terminated under sub-section (1), fresh proceedings shall be commenced in
accor dance with the provisions of this Act as if for a new election.

17. Postponement etc under
certain circumstances------Where proceedings relating to nomination,
scrutiny or withdrawal cannot, for reasons beyond the control of the Returning

such proceedings and shall, by public notice, fix another day for the
proceedings so postponed or adjourned and, if necessary, also the day or days

CHAPTER II

18 Uncontested------(1)
Where after scrutiny under section 8 or withdrawal under section 9, only one
person remains as a validly nominat ed candidate and his candidature is not
required to be approved, or, if so required, has been approved, under Article
166, or where after retirement under section 15, only one person is left as a
contesting candidate, the Returning Officer shall declare by public notice such
candidate to be elected to the office of President and send a return of the
election to the Commission:
Provided that if after scrutiny
any candidate indicates that he intends to make an appeal under sub-section (5)
of section 8 against the rejection of his nomination paper, no person shall be
declared elected uncontested until the period prescribed for filing such appeal
has expired and no such appeal has been filed, or, where an appeal is filed,
until the disposal of such appeal.
(2) The Commission shall publish
in the official Gazette the name of the returned candidate and also intimate
the name to the President's Secretariat.

20. Election agents-------(1)
Every candidate may appoint a person, not being a person disqualified to be an
election agent for election to the National Assembly or a Provincial Assembly,
to be his election agent ; and if no such appointment is made, he shall be
deemed to be his own election agent.
(2) The appointment of an
election agent under sub-section (1) may at any time be revoked in writing by
the candidate and, when it is so revoked or tote election agent dies, such
candidate may appoint another person in place of such election agent.
(3) Where an election agent is
appointed under sub-section (1) or sub-section (2), the candidate shall send a
notice in writing of the appointment, containing the name, father's name and
address of the election agent, to the Returning Officer.
(4) Every election agent shall
have an office at the address indicated in the notice sent under sub-section
(3) to which all notices and documents may be sent and any notice or document
addressed to the election agent and sent to such office shall be deemed to have
been served on, or delivered to, the election agent.

A contesting candidate or his election agent may before the commencement of the
poll, appoint not more than two polling agents to act at each polling station,
and give notice thereof in writing to the presiding officer.
(2) The appointment of a polling

polling agent, and give notice thereof in terms of sub-section (1).

24. Presiding officer and
polling officers-------(1) The Returning Officer shall appoint for each
poll ing station a presiding officer and such number of polling officers to
assist the presiding officer as the Returning Officer may consi der necessary.
(2) A presiding officer shall
conduct the poll in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the rules
and be responsible for maintaining order at the polling station.
(3) The presiding officer may,
during the course of the poll, entrust such of his functions as may be
specified by him to any polling officer and it shall be the duty of such
polling officer to perform the functions so entrusted.
(4) The Returning Officer shall
authorise one of the poll ing officers to act in place of the presiding officer
if the presiding officer is, at any time during the poll, through illness or
other cause, not present at the polling station, or is unable to perform his
functions and any absence of the presiding officer, and the reasons therefor,
shall, as soon as possible after the close of the poll, be reported to the
Returning Officer.
(5) The Returning Officer may, at
any time during the poll, for reasons to be recorded in writing, suspend any
presiding officer or polling officer and make such arrangements as he may
consider necessary for the performance of the functions of the officer so
suspended.

27. Adjourned poll-----(1)
If, at any time, the poll at any polling station is interrupted or obstructed
for reasons beyond the control of the presiding officer, he shall stop the poll
and inform the Returning Officer that he has done so.
(2) Where a poll is stopped under
sub-section (1), the Re turning Officer shall-
(a) immediately
report the circumstances to the Com mission ;
(b) as soon as
may be, appoint, with the approval of the Commission, a day for a fresh poll ;
and
(c) fix the
place at which and the hours during which such fresh poll shall be taken.
(3) All electors shall be allowed
to vote at the fresh poll under sub-section (2), and no vote cast of the poll
stopped under sub-section (1) shall be counted.

(d) so place the
ballot box within his sight in the polling station as to be ready to receive
the ballot papers.
(5) if one ballot box is full or
cannot further be used for receiving ballot papers, the presiding officer shall
seal the ballot box and use another ballot box in the manner laid down in sub
section (4).
